comment: I took Minds and Machines (CS101) years ago. I took it because it wasn't math, and while I wasn't sure what to think at first, this class is FAR ahead of its time. Over the years, as the digital revolution continues to unfold at unnerving speed, I've seen pretty much everything Dr. Charlesworth talked about come to fruition. For deep thinkers!

Lectures can be confusing and rambling. He easily gets lost on tangents. It's a fairly easy class, but the actual class-time can be VERY tedious. He assigns quizzes weekly. He is clearly passionate about the subject, but it can be difficult to share his enthusiasm. Homework can be confusing/pointless but some of the concepts are interesting.

The beginning lessons taught you how computers work not just how to code. Be prepared to code on paper and be extremely bored in labs and lectures are awful. He rants and rants about nonsense (he claims its not nonsense). If you have some decent background knowledge, I would take him, but if you don't, definitely don't take him if you can avoid it.

His compsci/neuro concepts are meaningfully applicable to other areas of life if you are passionate about the class, but unfortunately lectures are boring (rambling), incredibly convoluted even when it matters (e.g. you need definitions or have questions but he gives unhelpful answers), quizzes almost daily, $220 (!!) books. I would not recommend

Do not under any circumstances take a Charlesworth class. If you do, be prepared to listen to rants and rambles on random unrelated topics, boring lectures, and to spend an obscene amount of money on textbooks that he wrote himself. There are quizzes almost every class. Could not recommend less.

Charlesworth is the worst prof I've ever had at UR, he's literally senile- goes off of tangents that have absolutely nothing to do with the course and has the most confusing grading system. Gives quizzes every single day & made us buy $140 worth of books THAT HE WROTE HIMSELF. Save yourself and never take a class with this man.

Dr. Charlesworth is clearly passionate about what he teaches and means well. However, he is just a bad professor. His lectures have seemingly no connection to the class, he rambles on and on. To do well in this class  you have to be able to teach yourself the material. Quizzes every class. He assigns tedius homework and sometimes readings

If you are passionate about CS there is no better teacher to take for CS150. You will learn a lot about CS but will also learn a lot about how the mind works and how to optimize your learning. All this to say don't take this professor if your lazy and looking for an easy class. Take Charlesworth if you want to learn.

Do not take him unless you are looking to go far in Comp Sci and will take this course very seriously To the average student, take anyone else He will not tell you your grade in the course, and gives you a grade based on how you compare to your classmates He rambles all class about nonsense and gives off the persona of a caring guy but is not

Dr. C is an amazing professor whose hard work and dedication to the subjects and students are truly inspiring. His classes are hard, and he is a hard grader, but all the requirements are always extremely well written. He asks for understanding the material rather than memorizing it, and if you carefully study you will learn a lot.

Want to know why the ratings are so divided on this page? Because the sheep love Charlesworth. He openly tries to control your entire life and gives way more work than he's allowed to. Quiz every single class. The university is pulling him off the course because they got so many complaints from smart students who also have lives outside of class.

This is a two credit course. Dr. C has stated that it should be treated as a two credit course. If you do everything he tells you then you will learn a lot and you will pass. I've had Dr. C twice and him along with a few other specific professors at Richmond make me feel very confident about working after graduating.

Charlesworth is a top-notch professor and brilliant guy but also a goofball. Analogies and stories will be frequent, most are quite good. Relatively high volume, you'll learn a lot as a beginner or novice. He's been around since the start of computers, he has learned how to teach them. Take his class if you can think on the spot.

I have been in school for 15 years, and in that time have had 85-90 teachers. Without a fraction of a doubt, Charlesworth is by far the worst. Maybe he once was good, but frankly has entirely lost it. He rambles about nothing, talks over students when they ask questions, and brags constantly about himself. He makes CS tedious and overcomplicated.

Arthur Charlesworth is an awful professor. He goes on tangents about things that have nothing to do with the material. He does not explain anything and expects us to take homework quizzes every class. He does not answer our questions. It feels like he does not care about any of his students or their success. Do not take his class.

Art Charlesworth is the worst professor in America. The class began with 17 students and since dwindled to 10. The difficulty of this class is far too hard for an introductory class. He has clearly lost his mind and is not fit to teach at the university. We have a quiz in every single class session on the homework. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROF!!!!!!!!!!!

Dr. C is a very confusing man. For instance, during this semester he has said: "I had no idea that a lion had four legs." "Why is it that a whale can't fly?" "When I use a hammer, it doesn't mean the hammer is on the shelf, it means I'm hammering something with it." He can't teach well. I personally hated the class. If you decide to take it, GL.

Dr. Charlesworth rambles a lot in class, but so long as you can ignore his ramblings and focus on the course material he's teaching and do your assignments, you'll walk away with a very strong CS foundation. He grades assignments very quickly and puts a lot of effort into preparing for each class, so you'll get lots of helpful feedback.

Does not teach anything, literally! Quizzes you on stuff he hasn't taught! I'm good at computer science, but this man needs to understand I took the course not for life wisdom or applications of ML, but to actually learn it. You're better off watching Andrew Ng's videos for free, not worth your money or time, take time in the summer to learn this.

Dr. Charlesworth is indeed a respected and knowledgable professor. If you want to major in CS, take him. If not, do not take him. My interest in furthering my CS study ends at him. He makes CS so much harder than it is, but it is useful for your future CS study. There is lots of reading and preparation to do before class.

Dr. Charlesworth is whom a cs professor should be. He puts a lot of effort & time into making resources & material in order to effectively teach the class & give students' a cogent understanding of cs. He is willing to clarify concepts and respects students' confidence in cs. However, as always, you need to put the effort. Definitely recommend him.

Not a great professor. He is very, very, very wordy. Half of the test time is spend deciphering his language. Inconsistent grading (deducted points for no reason). Gives very hard tests. Keeps you late every lecture. Assigns hours of lab work per week. Never gives clear examples. Overall lack of clarity and structure to the course. Ruined my GPA.

Charlesworth was probably one of the best professors that I've encountered at Richmond thus far. Yes, sometimes he can be dry and use a lot of unfamiliar vocabulary, but he is good at relaying information at is very helpful inside and outside of the classroom. He really peaked my interest in Comp Sci and I recommend you take him.

He is the worst professor.. I have a high interest in computer science before I took the class and he completely ruin my interest. Every class, he spend almost twenty minutes talk about non-CS related thing. He sent three eamile per day on average and all of them are extremely wordy. He's wasting my time for the entire semester! AVOID HIM!

He is probably the best professor I have ever had. He explains everything clearly, goes deep into details, and grades fairly. His tests could be quite tricky and hard to get perfect scores, but he gives a lot of bonus points. Take his class if you can.

Charlesworth is one of the clearest professors you will encounter. He spends hours preparing for class in order to guarantee your understanding. There is a small amount of hmwk for every class, worth ~10 pts each. Every few weeks, there's a quiz or test. He relies heavily on his self-created exercise booklet, not the textbook. Definitely recommend!

One of the most intelligent professors I have ever had.  Puts hours and hours into the class and it really shows because he is truly an expert in what he teaches. Pretty funny and quirky guy, not too hard also.  The only thing is he sometimes has a tough time "dumbing down" the material because of his mastery of the subject.

Great Professor, Minds and Machines was one of the easier class I took @ UR, but it is necessary to remain diligent w/ the hwk. He's really helpful, and takes attendance seriously. He creates packets for students who miss class.

Charlesworth is one of the best profs at this university by far... the only problem I've had is that he goes too slow sometimes so that those in the class who aren't getting it have lots of reiteration. He went over an entire lesson for me in his office because I had to miss the first day of class, and that's only the beginning. He's just adorable.

I thought his class was super easy, but I had taken calc before... Still, i know that others who had also taken calc before were struggling in this class. You just have to know how to take his quizzes/tests-how he thinks. He may be quirky, but you can tell he's a brilliant man, and WAY nice. No matter what you say, he cares about his students a ton

Charlesworth truly cares about YOUR LEARNING!! He is so into teaching, and is readily available to give you extra help whenever you need it. He wants to see your improvement. He is down to earth, but a little strange at times. Once the lights went out so he had with him a light on a headband which he proceeded to use to teach the class-funny man!

Dr. Charlesworth is hilarious and... oh, just got another email from the Charlesmeister himself.  Oh yeah, he'll fill up your email inbox with emails; they're helpful but no, I don't read all of them and I prolly should.  Has a good system for grading, doesn't collect homework; instead has daily quizzes.  Eccentric, amusing, helpful, but difficult.
Best professor I had at UR. If you are at all mathematically inclined, take his classes.

worst teacher i've ever had....He made me hate calculus and mathematics in general.. his lectures do not make sense and his teaching principles are horrible. Don't take this teacher for Calculus..he may be good for other subjects..but definetly not for calculus. I received a very bad grade from him even though math is usually my strongest subject.
Amazing professor!

of all the professors i've had, he's the best at makin you feel like you're getting your money's worth....i got into the class after the first session had met and he called me and taught me the material over the phone.....great teacher, and the class isnt too bad, but there's work every night ...just requires a some effort, interesting stuff though
he sucked...he cant teach or translate the material to the students...he makes everything harder than it needed to be..

This guy is obviously a genius and has a very good reputation but I don't know if this necessarily translates into him being a good professor.  He makes things so much more difficult than they need to be.  I got the worst class of my college career in his class (C+), although my calc skills are not that great.
Best teacher I have ever had. If you are a math-minded person then you will like his teaching style. He is motivating and will hold you to high standards. You will have to work hard.
No Comments
Dr. Charlesworth is extremely accomodating and always willing to help.  His grading system seems fair albeit confusing.  Sometimes was unclear what he was talking about in class.

Very hard.  He also did not care that he was having us program a useless project in the engineering course.  He also did not take into consideration the unfairness of the teams he selected.  This is not a guy you want to take if you plan on working in the real business world.
His lectures are clear, and he is extremely willing to help.  He is also a great person, and one of the best professors I have ever had.
I have graduated but Dr. Charlesworth was the best professor I ever had at University of Richmond. Challenging, Interesting and Extremely fair.
Unhelpful, arrogant, and rude.  Discouraged me from taking any interest in mathematics.  I am now an accounting major.
Dr. Charlesworth is exceptional. He's thorough, clear, and extremely fair.
